newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria against strict stability pact - Vranitzky.
newsitem.headline: Austria against strict stability pact - Vranitzky.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday he was opposed to introducing automatic sanctions against countries that failed to comply with the Maastricht criteria for Europe's single currency.
"Austria is against automatic sanctions in the case of non-compliance with the Maastricht stability criteria," Vranitzky told a news conference ahead of Friday's European Union summit in Dublin.

Germany has insisted a proposed stability pact for the euro must include set penalties for exceeding the criteria, which set strict thresholds for membership in the single currency in terms of debt, deficit, inflation, and exchange and interest rates.
"Sanctions should be decided on a political basis and not automatically," Vranitzky said.
The chancellor said he thought it unlikely the Dublin Summit would reach a final decision on the stability pact.
"According to our latest information, one should be careful with such expectations," he said. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
